statement: A running model, not a calibrated one, and thinner than the wisteria model it began from. What the plant is made of (opposite leaves of a measured length, cymes on short side shoots from older stems, paired follicles that seldom set in Britain, the weeks it flowers) follows floras, the RHS and one three-year study of a ten-year-old plant on a pergola in Belgrade; how far its shoots hold themselves out in the air and how stiff they are at the base follow measurements of its searcher shoots (Vecchiato et al. 2023). How fast it grows, how thickly it clothes a lattice, how its leaves and twigs are held and how much of it flowers are assumptions chosen to agree with those descriptions and with photographs; none has been measured on a plant in Britain. The numbers by which a shoot chooses its way over a structure are still the wisteria model's. Use its output to compare scenarios and to show what a design implies, not to predict dates, sizes or loads.

names.basis: One leaf form and one flower form, so none is named. The cymes stand out from the foliage on slender stalks 2 to 6 cm long (Flora of China), at the ends and in the upper leaf axils of short side shoots (Bean: 'usually on short lateral twigs'). The paired follicles hang: seen in photographs of fruiting plants (Wikimedia Commons, 'Fruit du faux jasmin'), not stated in a flora.

phenology.budburstDoy.basis: No dated British record of the start of growth was found. Placed in mid April (15 April) so that the year's first shoots are full grown by mid June, which is when a three-year study in Belgrade found shoots at 90% of their length with leaves fully open (Ocokoljic et al. 2026, Pak. J. Bot. 58(7), BBCH 39).

phenology.growthEndDoy.basis: Long twining shoots go on being made after flowering, through late summer; growth is taken to stop at the end of September. No dated source.

phenology.leafFlushDoy.basis: An evergreen: this only paces the opening of leaves on wood that was already there. New leaves from late April to mid June; the end is the Belgrade study's date for fully expanded leaves (Ocokoljic et al. 2026), which Britain may run later than.

phenology.autumnColourDoy.basis: Not acted on: the engine gives an evergreen leaf no change of colour. Recorded as the weeks in which the leaves take their winter bronze and red with the first cold (RHS: 'often turning deep bronze-red in winter'), mid November to mid December, for when it can be shown.

phenology.leafFallDoy.basis: Not acted on for an evergreen: a leaf stays for organs.leafLifespanYears. Kept at the end of the year only because every model carries the parameter.

phenology.floralInitiationDoy.basis: Flower buds are taken to show on the young side shoots from the start of June, a month before the first open. In photographs the cymes stand in green bud for weeks before any flower opens. No dated source.

phenology.flowerOpenDoy.basis: Cymes begin to open from the end of June to about 10 August, so that with the weeks each lasts the plant is in flower through July and August: Bean, 'produced in July and August'; RHS, 'mid to late summer'. In Belgrade the first tenth of the flowers were open on day 161 to 168 and the last petals fell on day 227 to 233 in two ordinary years (Ocokoljic et al. 2026); Britain is cooler, and the later British months are kept.

phenology.petalFallDoy.basis: Not acted on while phenology.flowerLastsDays is given: each cyme then goes over in its own time. Set to the span in which they do.

phenology.flowerLastsDays.basis: How long one cyme is in flower: its two to nine flowers (counted in Belgrade, Ocokoljic et al. 2026) open a few at a time. Chosen so that the whole plant flowers for about nine weeks, as it did there in two ordinary years (66 and 65 days from the first tenth open to the last petal fallen). Not timed on a single cyme.

extension.leaderMPerSeason.basis: RHS guide: 'It is relatively slow growing, but in favourable conditions can eventually reach 4m (14ft) or more.' Bean has it 10 or 12 ft high on walls in the south and west, and 'rather slow-growing when young'. The RHS record's band of 8 to 12 m in 5 to 10 years would need more than a metre a year and is not what British growers report; one retailer's 10 to 20 cm a year is slower than plants that fill a fence panel in five years. 0.7 m takes a main stem to the top of a 3 m support in its fifth or sixth season. Not measured.

extension.lateralMPerSeasonByOrder.basis: Side branches a little slower than the main stems, each order slower again. Scaled from the leader rate; not measured. With the branching above they clothe about 2 m by 2 m of lattice by the fifth or sixth season, which is what one grower reports of a plant in Gloucestershire (6.5 ft by 6 ft after five years, growsonyou.com question 27963): an anecdote, used as a check and not as a source.

extension.whipMPerSeason.basis: The long twining shoots that an established plant throws out from its older stems in summer, which reach for something to wind round. They make their length within the season. Rate not measured.

extension.establishmentFactorByYear.basis: Slow to start. Bean: 'It is rather slow-growing when young'. The RHS guide has plants established after two or three years, when they 'will be hardier than recently planted ones'; Useful Temperate Plants, citing Davis, warns that they 'may put on no new growth for the first 2 - 3 years after planting out'. Three seasons of reduced extension, the first at under a third. The factors themselves are not measured.

architecture.trunkStemStartYears.basis: A nursery plant comes as several stems tied to canes (RHS guide: 'usually trained onto bamboo canes'), and an established one goes on sending shoots from the base: three stems from the first season, two more in the second and one in the third. The number is a choice.

architecture.nurseryCaneM.basis: RHS guide: nursery plants 'vary in height from about 60cm (2ft) to 1.8m (6ft) or more'. A plant from the lower half of that range.

architecture.maxBranchOrder.basis: Branches of branches of branches run along the lattice before the short flowering shoots take over: one order more than the wisteria model, for a plant that makes a mat of fine stems rather than a few thick ones. A choice.

architecture.leaderLengthM.basis: A cap on the length of a main stem: from the RHS guide's '4m (14ft) or more' to the RHS record's 'about 9m in height'. A height is not a route length, so this is a stand-in.

architecture.lateralLengthMByOrder.basis: Side branches run for metres: the RHS record gives a spread of 4 to 8 m. Scaled down by order; not measured.

architecture.lateralLengthSpread.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

architecture.lateralChanceByParentOrder.basis: It branches freely and 'will cover its support effectively on its own, twining and scrambling up and across' (RHS guide), so nearly every crossing of the lattice that a stem passes sends a branch along the other member. The chances are a choice.

architecture.budExtraDormancyChance.basis: Most buds left at a crossing of the lattice break the next spring: the plant branches freely and fills in behind its leading shoots ('will cover its support effectively on its own', RHS guide). One in five waits longer. A choice, not a count.

architecture.budExtraDormancyYears.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

architecture.maxStemsPerRoute.basis: Its slender stems wind round one another as well as round the support, so a lath or a cable carries a rope of several: seen in photographs of established plants (Wikimedia Commons, Starr 090416-5994 and 'Trachelospermum jasminoides A'). Four is a choice; not counted on plants.

architecture.maxStemsPerPrimaryMember.basis: One more than on a lath, as in the wisteria model, a glulam member being wide enough to lay more stems side by side.

routing.occupancyCost.basis: How much a shoot is put off a member that already carries stems. The wisteria model's figure, kept here for a different reason: a gardener training a young plant spreads its stems over the support rather than letting them rope up one wire (RHS guide: young plants 'may need some guiding and tying in until they're able to twine'). At half this (the earlier choice) every stem of a young plant went up the one cable stay of the specimen frame. A choice; nothing measured.

routing.downhillCostPerM.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.uphillBonusPerM.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.straightOnBonus.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.riserBonus.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.tierBonus.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.roleDropChance.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.noise.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

routing.giveUpCost.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

attachment.maxGraspDiameterMm.basis: No measurement exists. Taken as well below the timber lattice (76 mm round) and above a cable, so that this plant twines cables unaided and has to be tied to glulam. The whole difference between it and wisteria on the structure rests on this number. What is recorded: it is sold wound on bamboo canes, and the RHS guide asks for a support of wires or trellis and says 'Young plants may need some guiding and tying in until they're able to twine'.

attachment.minPitchM.basis: The rise of one turn round a thin support. Read off a photograph of stems on a bamboo cane (Wikimedia Commons, 'Trachelospermum jasminoides A'), where a turn takes several widths of the cane: a slack spiral, tighter than the wisteria model's 0.3 m because the stems are far more slender. Not measured.

attachment.pitchPerCircumference.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

organs.leafSpacingM.basis: The length between leaf pairs on the long twining shoots and the framework they become: 5 to 10 cm, read off photographs against the leaf lengths the floras give (Commons, 'Trachelospermum jasminoides RHu 01', 'Trachelospermum jasminoides en hiver'). No flora gives it. The short flowering twigs, which carry most of the foliage, have their own spacing (organs.sideShootLeafSpacingM). The engine sets a node only at a stored point of a stem, 4 cm apart.

organs.leafLengthM.basis: Ocokoljic et al. 2026, Pak. J. Bot. 58(7): 300 full-grown leaves of a ten-year-old plant on a pergola in Belgrade measured 4.20 to 8.80 cm long. The same species, cultivated outdoors in a climate with colder winters and hotter summers than Britain's; whether the stalk (3 to 12 mm, Flora of China) was included is not said. Flora of China gives the blade as 2 to 10 cm, Bean as 1 1/2 to 3 1/2 in.

organs.leavesPerNode.basis: NC State Extension plant record: leaf arrangement 'Opposite'. The Belgrade study says the same of the leaves it measured.

organs.spurChance.basis: It makes no spurs. The short leafy shoots that clothe its older stems and carry its flowers are grown as flowering side shoots (sideShoots.*), which bear their leaves in pairs along their length; a spur in this engine is wisteria's, a tuft at one node that hangs clear of the timber.

organs.spurLengthM.basis: Not acted on while organs.spurChance is 0; present because every model carries every parameter.

organs.spurLeafCount.basis: Not acted on while organs.spurChance is 0; present because every model carries every parameter.

organs.racemeLengthM.basis: The width of the cluster of flowers at the end of a cyme's stalk, which is what the flower model is authored to. Two to nine flowers (counted in Belgrade, Ocokoljic et al. 2026), each 1.7 to 2.3 cm across (measured there), standing loosely on forks 1 to 2 cm long, make a cluster two to four flowers wide. No source measures the cluster itself; Bean's cymes of 1 1/2 to 2 in. and Flora of China's stalk of 2 to 6 cm are lengths, not widths.

organs.whipShareOfNodes.basis: The share of older leaf nodes that throw a long twining shoot in a year. Photographs of established plants in summer show such shoots standing out of the foliage every few hand-widths; the share is a choice.

organs.whipsPerYearMax.basis: A cap on new long shoots a year, so that a large plant does not bristle. A choice.

organs.whipLengthM.basis: How far a long shoot of the year grows when it finds nothing to wind round. Its searchers hold themselves out to about 1.1 m (Vecchiato et al. 2023); beyond that a shoot droops, hangs or winds round its neighbours. In photographs of established plants such shoots stand a few leaf lengths to an arm's length out of the foliage (Commons, 'Star Jasmine ... Capel Manor ... 01'). The range is a choice below the measured reach.

organs.leafLifespanYears.basis: Evergreen and leathery, but no source read says how long a leaf lives. Three seasons assumed; older leaves are seen yellowing and reddening before they fall, and cold may strip them sooner (RHS guide: in cold snaps 'the leaves may turn red, develop spots or even fall').

organs.clearStemHeightM.basis: Clothed nearly to the ground while young; side shoots are not thrown from the lowest hand-width of stem. A choice.

flowering.competenceYears.basis: Nursery plants are sold in flower, so it flowers young. In the model its first flowering side shoots break from the cane it arrived with in its second season.

flowering.maturityRamp.basis: Flowering builds up while the plant establishes, which the RHS guide puts at two or three years; but it flowers freely young: nursery plants are sold in flower, and a plant about two metres tall is covered in it (photograph, Wikimedia Commons, 'Jasmin-rue-Judaique (1)'). The steps are a choice.

flowering.spurFloralChance.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

flowering.unprunedFactor.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

flowering.currentSeasonFlowersPerM.basis: Cymes in the leaf axils of the year's long growth. Flora of China has the cymes 'terminal and axillary', and photographs show them at several nodes in turn along a leafy shoot (Wikimedia Commons, 'Trachelospermum jasminoides RHu 01', 'Trachelospermum jasminoides 13zz'); Bean has them 'usually on short lateral twigs', so the long shoots carry fewer. Five to the metre, a cyme at one node in six, is a choice.

flowering.currentSeasonMinShootM.basis: A shoot shorter than this is taken not to flower in its leaf axils. A placeholder.

pruning.summerLeavesKept.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

pruning.winterBudsKept.basis: Not applicable to this plant; present because every model carries every parameter.

regrowth.shootsPerCut.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

thickening.tipRadiusSquaredMm2.basis: A young shoot about 2 mm thick behind its tip: read off photographs against leaves of known width (Commons, 'Fulles de gesmiler ... Altea', where the green shoots are about a twelfth of the width of a blade 1.6 to 3.4 cm wide; 'Trachelospermum jasminoides closeup'). No flora gives the thickness of a shoot.

thickening.radiusSquaredPerMetreMm2.basis: Stems stay slender: chosen so that the main stems of a ten-year-old plant on the specimen frame are about as thick as a thumb at the base. No measured stem diameters were found.

thickening.branchShare.basis: Copied from the Wisteria sinensis model for want of anything better. Not a measurement or a description of this plant.

fruit.setShare.basis: RHS guide: 'fruits (and seeds) are rarely produced in UK gardens'; in Belgrade none set in three years (Ocokoljic et al. 2026). One cyme in a hundred and twenty-five is this model's reading of 'rarely': two or three pairs of pods in a year on a plant that covers a fence panel, a dozen or so on one that covers a wall, a young plant usually having none.

fruit.lengthM.basis: Flora of China, volume 16 (efloras.org taxon 200018474, read from the copy at this address because efloras.org refused the request): follicles linear, 10 to 25 cm long and 3 to 10 mm wide. One fruit here is the pair of follicles that follows one flower.

fruit.swellDays.basis: Days for the follicles to reach their length after the flower goes over. No source times it; chosen so that pods from August flowers are full length by late autumn.

fruit.ripenDoy.basis: Flora of China: 'Fl. Mar-Aug, fr. Jun-Dec.', in China. In Britain it flowers three months later than it begins to there; the green pods are taken to turn brown in December. No British record of ripening was found.

fruit.fallDoy.basis: The dry follicles split along one side and let their plumed seeds go; taken to happen from mid January to mid March, so that pods hang through the winter. Not recorded for Britain.

appendages.tendrilNodePattern.basis: It has no tendrils: a twiner that holds on with its stems (RHS: 'with twining stems'). No description read mentions any.

appendages.leafStalkCoilShare.basis: Its leaf stalks are 3 to 12 mm long (Flora of China) and do not clasp: it holds on with its stems.

appendages.prickleSpacingM.basis: Unarmed: no description read mentions prickles or thorns.

sideShoots.bearingWoodAgeYears.basis: The flowering shoots break from wood made in earlier years: Useful Temperate Plants, citing Huxley's RHS Dictionary of Gardening, 'Flowers are produced on short laterals that grow from old wood'; Bean, 'usually on short lateral twigs'; Clemson Extension has them on short side branches. Last year's stems are old enough.

sideShoots.perMetrePerYear.basis: How thickly the older stems are set with short flowering shoots. At the leaf spacing above this puts one at nearly every leaf node of a stem a year old or more that has none: photographs of established plants show the older stems hidden by leafy twigs, and a lattice it has covered reads as a screen (the RHS lists hedging and screens among its uses). Not counted on plants.

sideShoots.lengthM.basis: 'Short lateral twigs' (Bean): one to six pairs of leaves 2 to 4 cm apart below the cyme in photographs, two fingers' width to a hand-span and a bit (Commons, 'Trachelospermum jasminoides RHu 01', 'Trachelospermum jasminoides closeup'). The range is kept wide so that the twigs along a stem are of unequal length, as they are on the plant. Not measured.

sideShoots.lifespanYears.basis: The short shoots are woody and stay: on the plant they branch again and flower from their own side shoots in later years, which this model shows as the same shoot flowering again. Four seasons is a choice, a little longer than a leaf is taken to last.

sideShoots.terminalFlowerShare.basis: Nine in ten of the short shoots of an established plant end in a cyme in a year. In photographs of plants in full flower hardly a shoot is without one: a young plant two metres tall on a wall in Bordeaux (Wikimedia Commons, 'Jasmin-rue-Judaique (1)'), a plant in a London garden ('Star Jasmine Trachelospermum Jasminoides Capel Manor College Gardens Enfield London England 01') and a fence in New Orleans ('Jasmine covered fence, New Orleans April 2026') are white with them. The share is a choice read from those pictures, and takes no account of shade, which the profiles say reduces flowering. Not counted on plants.

mechanics.searcherReachM.basis: Vecchiato, Hattermann, Palladino, Tedone, Heuret, Rowe and Marcati 2023, PLoS Computational Biology 19:e1011538: searcher shoots of Trachelospermum jasminoides and of Condylocarpon guianense reach 'similar maximal reach capacities of around 110 cm in length' (five searchers of each measured). Hattermann et al. 2022 (https://doi.org/10.3389/ffgc.2022.836247) list it among 29 climbers and give twiners 10 to 225 cm. Measured on searchers of plants grown in France, not in Britain.

mechanics.woodModulusMPa.basis: Vecchiato et al. 2023: the two species have 'similar values of structural Young's modulus at the base of searcher shoots of around 3000'; the paper prints the unit as N m-2 in that sentence and as MN/m2 in its methods, and 3000 MN/m2 (= MPa) is the reading that agrees with Hattermann et al. 2022 (213 to 15 479 MN/m2 across 29 climbers). The base of a searcher is its stiffest, oldest stretch: taken for wood that has set.

mechanics.greenShootModulusMPa.basis: Not measured for this plant. A tenth of the measured base of its searchers (Vecchiato et al. 2023, about 3000 MN/m2), near the least stiff searcher base Hattermann et al. 2022 measured among 29 climbers (213 MN/m2): the soft, latex-filled growing end of a twiner's searcher is far less stiff than its base.

mechanics.woodSetDays.basis: How long a new stretch of shoot stays soft. Not measured. In photographs the year's shoots are green and pliant for a hand-span or two behind the tip and brown and woody below (Wikimedia Commons, 'Trachelospermum jasminoides RHu 01', 'Fulles de gesmiler ... Altea'); at the summer growth rate of a few centimetres a week that is six weeks or so.

mechanics.stemFreshDensityKgM3.basis: Not weighed. A young shoot is mostly water and latex: the density of water, as Chelakkot and Mahadevan 2017 take for a young shoot (https://doi.org/10.1098/rsif.2017.0001).

mechanics.leafFreshMassPerAreaKgM2.basis: Not weighed. The leaf is leathery (Flora of China: 'leathery or nearly so'), a blade roughly 0.4 mm thick by eye in photographs: 0.4 kg to the square metre, twice the generic thin leaf. The engine takes a leaf as a disc 0.56 of its length across; for this elliptic blade, about 0.4 as wide as long, that disc is close to the blade's own area, so no allowance is made for the outline.

mechanics.inflorescenceFreshMassKg.basis: Not weighed. Two to nine flowers (Ocokoljic et al. 2026) each a corolla about 2 cm across of thin petals on a tube 5 to 10 mm long, with a stalk 2 to 6 cm (Flora of China): a gram and a half for the cyme is an estimate from its size.

mechanics.fruitFreshMassKg.basis: Not weighed. Two follicles 10 to 25 cm long and 3 to 10 mm thick (Flora of China), slender and tapering: each about 3 cm3 of tissue at the middle sizes, so about 6 g for the pair green.

mechanics.leanDeg.basis: The least a free shoot leans from plumb where it leaves its support. Vecchiato et al. 2023 start their model of a Trachelospermum jasminoides searcher at pi/4 (45 degrees) from the vertical; that is a modelling choice of theirs, not a measurement. Photographs show the long shoots of the year leaving the plant at every angle from nearly upright to level (Commons, 'Star Jasmine ... Capel Manor ... 01', 'Trachelospermum jasminoides RHu 01'). Thirty degrees is a choice between.

mechanics.leafWeightOffsetShare.basis: Where a leaf's weight hangs off the stem. The stalk is short (3 to 12 mm, Flora of China) and the blade elliptic, widest about the middle, so the blade's centre of mass is a little past half the leaf's length. Not measured.

tropism.turnPerM.basis: How sharply a searcher turns to the direction it seeks. Not measured. Vecchiato et al. 2023 fit an active posture control to T. jasminoides searchers but give its strength in their own model's terms, not as a turn per metre. A weak pull, a little under the generic shoot's, for a twiner whose searchers lean and sweep and are seen arching over and hanging in photographs rather than standing plumb.

tropism.lightShare.basis: A plant of the sunny edges of forests and brushwood (Flora of China) that accepts partial shade (RHS): its searchers are taken to seek a direction a little nearer up than the light. A choice.

attachment.graspReachM.basis: How near the tip of a searcher must come to a support to wind on to it. Not measured for this plant. Darwin 1875 (https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/2485) saw the revolving shoots of twiners sweep circles from about 0.5 m (hop) to over 1.5 m across; a quarter of the hop's sweep, the generic figure, is kept for a slender twiner whose tip revolves less widely than a hop's.

sideShoots.branchAngleDeg.basis: The angle at which the short leafy twigs leave their stem, from the axil of a leaf of an opposite pair. Read off photographs of established plants on walls and frames: they leave at a half to most of a right angle and bend over under their leaves and cymes (Commons, 'Trachelospermum jasminoides RHu 01', 'Trachelospermum jasminoides en hiver'). Not measured.

sideShoots.breakSpreadDays.basis: The twigs break over about five weeks from the start of growth, so that they are all in leaf by mid June, when the Belgrade study found shoots at 90 per cent of their length (Ocokoljic et al. 2026, BBCH 39). Not timed.

sideShoots.startTowardsLight.basis: The twigs on a wall or frame turn out and up to the light as they set out, but stay in their pairs and are not all upright: in photographs they stand at every angle off the stems and the plant reads as a mat, not a brush (Commons, 'Trachelospermum jasminoides RHu 01'). A choice.

organs.alternateDivergenceDeg.basis: The leaves are opposite (NC State Extension; Ocokoljic et al. 2026), the pairs at right angles to one another (decussate) as in the dogbane family generally and in photographs; the engine uses this angle only where leaves stand singly, so it is given for completeness and does not act on this plant.

sideShoots.baseDiameterMm.basis: A twig a hand-span long is about 3 mm thick at its base, read off photographs against leaves of known width (Commons, 'Fulles de gesmiler ... Altea'). No flora gives it.

sideShoots.extensionMPerYear.basis: The short shoots stay and grow on: in later years they lengthen and throw short shoots of their own that flower (Useful Temperate Plants, citing Huxley: flowers on 'short laterals that grow from old wood'). The engine lets a side shoot lengthen but not fork; five to fifteen centimetres a year stands for both. Not measured.

sideShoots.maxLengthM.basis: The mat of twigs on an established plant is a hand-span or two deep and fills the space between laths 0.4 m apart in photographs of plants on trellis and fences (Commons, 'Trachelospermum jasminoides RHu 01', 'Star Jasmine ... Capel Manor ... 01'). A choice.

organs.leafTurnToOpenShare.basis: The leaf stalks turn their blades out from the wall or frame to the light, keeping the pairs, so that a plant on a wall is a sheet of overlapping faces (Commons, 'Trachelospermum jasminoides RHu 01', 'Fulles de gesmiler ... Altea'). A choice read from photographs.

phenology.evergreenLeafFallDoy.basis: When a leaf at the end of its life falls. No dated source. Old leaves are seen yellow and red through the winter and spring (Commons, 'Trachelospermum jasminoides en hiver'; RHS growing guide, in cold snaps the leaves 'may turn red, develop spots or even fall') and are taken to drop once the new leaves are opening, from mid May to the end of June, so that the plant is never bare: an evergreen that sheds its oldest leaves behind the new flush. The window begins after phenology.leafFlushDoy does.

organs.sideShootLeafSpacingM.basis: The short flowering twigs are close-jointed, 2 to 4 cm between pairs, in photographs (Commons, 'Trachelospermum jasminoides RHu 01', 'Trachelospermum jasminoides closeup'). Not measured. The engine's stored points are 4 cm apart, so on a twig a pair stands at every point.

organs.sideShootLeavesPerNode.basis: NC State Extension: leaf arrangement 'Opposite', on every shoot.

organs.sideShootLeafLifespanYears.basis: As organs.leafLifespanYears: the leaves of a twig are taken to last three seasons, so that a twig that grows on is leafy at its outer end and bare at its base, as old twigs are in photographs. Not measured.
